annotationRationale: The decisive operation is regrouping equal values with opposite signs. Function substitution and multiplication laws establish equality, while odd-even parity establishes the opposite signs.

classificationReview.areaRationale: The sum is evaluated using an algebraic identity and cancellation, so Algebra replaces Unclassified.
classificationReview.areaCheck: Algebra is the correct subject repair because an algebraic identity and regrouping evaluate the sum.

review.questionCheck: Independently, \(f(x)=f(1-x)\), and complementary indices have opposite parity because their sum is 2019. All 2018 terms cancel in 1009 pairs, giving 0, choice A. The current question and choices are consistent.
review.alternativeMethodCheck: LIVE's complementary-index cancellation is retained. Random Math's function-symmetry pairing is merged into the same route, with its erroneous displayed regrouping signs corrected. No shared-bank methods are supplied, and another calculation would add no useful distinct approach.
review.annotationCheck: Addition properties are appropriately assessed. Function evaluation, multiplication laws, and parity support the equality and opposite signs. The function symmetry is derived explicitly and needs no additional catalog node.
review.areaCheck: Algebra is the correct subject repair because an algebraic identity and regrouping evaluate the sum.

methodReviews.mathCheck: Substitution gives \(f(1-x)=f(x)\). For each \(1\leq k\leq1009\), its partner \(2019-k\) lies between 1010 and 2018 and has opposite parity. These disjoint pairs cover every index exactly once, and each signed contribution is zero.
methodReviews.sourceMethodCheck: Both cited third-party references use this pairing. The candidate correctly preserves the original signs, unlike Random Math's displayed regrouping for even indices. The source-informed-original classification and reconstructed prose are appropriate.
methodReviews.pedagogyCheck: The opening explains why complementary inputs help. Equality, parity, and complete coverage of the indices are all justified, making the cancellation reconstructible.
methodReviews.directNodeCheck: cnm_011 covers regrouping; cnm_196 and cnm_015 support the substituted identity; cnm_p156 supports the parity argument. None is unsupported.

nativeLayerJudgments.CN: The four exact native-topic links fit their stated roles. The method exercises particular evaluation, operation-law, and parity skills without establishing every mastery criterion.
nativeLayerJudgments.US: The narrower 7.NS.A.1d and 7.NS.A.2c links fit rational rearrangement and multiplication properties. F-IF.A.2 supports substitution partially. The aggregate 7.NS.A.2 is broader than this work, and 7.NS.A.2a's contextual interpretation is absent. The partial 2.OA.C.3 link does not directly cover this parity argument with indices beyond 20.
nativeLayerJudgments.ailleo: All four immediate nodes are precise and used. The derived complementary-input identity is adequately explained from these elementary concepts.
